standard_prerequisites.name: The category C of systems with the comparison lemma for maps whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a fixed power of I

standard_prerequisites.use: Is the category in which the isomorphism is asserted and the tool that promotes bounded-annihilation maps to isomorphisms.

standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the constant c that makes the systems (K(n)) and (K_n) isomorphic.

core_obligations: Choose a presentation 0 -> K -> A^{oplus r} -> M -> 0, set K_n = K/I^nK, and define K(n) = Ker(A_n^{oplus r} -> M_n) so that 0 -> K(n) -> A_n^{oplus r} -> M_n -> 0 is exact and there are surjections K_n -> K(n) (proof lines 29213-29223).

Apply the Artin-Rees consequence lemma to get c >= 0 and maps K(n) -> K_n/I^{n-c}K_n that are almost inverse, and since I^{n-c}K_n is contained in K_n[I^c], conclude that the systems (K(n)) and (K_n) are isomorphic in the category C (proof lines 29223-29229).

Show that the systems {Ext^i_{A_n}(K(n), N_n)} and {Ext^i_{A_n}(K_n, N_n)} are isomorphic in C: the surjections K_n -> K(n) have kernels annihilated by I^c, so the induced maps on Ext have kernel and cokernel annihilated by I^c, and the comparison lemma applies (proof lines 29232-29244).
Use the shift isomorphisms Ext^{i-1}_A(K, N) = Ext^i_A(M, N) and the analogous isomorphism after reduction to deduce that it suffices to prove the lemma for i = 0 and i = 1 (proof lines 29247-29254).

Write down the commutative diagram comparing the two long exact sequences in degrees 0 and 1, involving Hom(M, N), N^{oplus r}, Hom(K, N), Ext^1(M, N) and their reduced analogues (proof lines 29257-29276).

Use the Mittag-Leffler comparison lemma to bound the kernel and cokernel of Hom(M, N)/I^n Hom(M, N) -> Hom(M_n, N_n) and of the analogous map for K by I^c-torsion, for a single constant c independent of n, and combine with the earlier annihilation statement to construct maps delta_n : I^c Hom(K, N)/I^n Hom(K, N) -> Hom(K(n), N_n) with kernel and cokernel annihilated by I^c after possibly increasing c (proof lines 29277-29289).

Use commutativity of the displayed solid diagram to define the dotted arrow I^c Ext^1(M, N)/I^n Ext^1(M, N) -> Ext^1(M_n, N_n), and conclude by the diagram chase, stated to be omitted, that its kernel and cokernel are annihilated by I^c after one final increase of c, which gives the required isomorphism in C (proof lines 29290-29304).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an ideal I in a Noetherian ring A and finite modules M and N, sets A_n = A/I^n, M_n = M/I^nM and N_n = N/I^nN, and asserts that for every i >= 0 the systems {Ext^i_A(M, N)/I^n Ext^i_A(M, N)} and {Ext^i_{A_n}(M_n, N_n)} are isomorphic in the category C of weird systems (source lines 29193-29210). The proof is a long comparison argument. It first chooses a presentation 0 -> K -> A^{oplus r} -> M -> 0, defines K_n = K/I^nK and K(n) = Ker(A_n^{oplus r} -> M_n), and uses the Artin-Rees consequence lemma to get a constant c and maps K(n) -> K_n/I^{n-c}K_n that are 'almost inverse', exhibiting an isomorphism of the systems (K(n)) and (K_n) in C (proof lines 29213-29229). It then proves the analogous statement for Ext groups: the surjections K_n -> K(n) have kernels annihilated by I^c, so the induced maps on Ext have kernel and cokernel annihilated by I^c, giving an isomorphism of the two Ext systems by the comparison lemma (proof lines 29232-29244). The proof then reduces to i = 0, 1 by the shift isomorphisms Ext^{i-1}_A(K, N) = Ext^i_A(M, N) and the analogous statement after reduction (proof lines 29247-29254). The substantive part is the final diagram chase for i = 0, 1: the proof writes down the commutative diagram comparing the two long exact sequences, uses the Mittag-Leffler comparison lemma to bound the kernel and cokernel of Hom(M, N)/I^n Hom(M, N) -> Hom(M_n, N_n) and of the analogous map for K by I^c-torsion, constructs maps delta_n between the I^c-saturated pieces, and finally makes a diagram chase (stated to be omitted) on the displayed solid diagram to define the dotted arrow and bound its kernel and cokernel (proof lines 29257-29304). The two-step reduction with Artin-Rees, the annihilation bookkeeping with a single constant c, and the final chase are independent research-level content.
